page: Amazon Web Services m9g.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an ARM64-based AWS Graviton processor built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz, with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU acceleration bundled with this instance, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m9g.2xlarge demonstrates strong memory and compression capabilities. It achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.45 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 16.84 GB/sec, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score of 4064.84. Average performance tiers are observed in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in static web serving throughput at 28.84 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 23.58 million operations per second. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in the PassMark CPU encryption test and medium-model LLM prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 Graviton architecture offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, making it a viable option for general-purpose workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or high-performance cryptography. The instance is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, memory-intensive caching, database operations, and lightweight single-threaded data compression tasks.
description: The Amazon Web Services m9g.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an ARM64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz and 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPU hardware, relying on a 4 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression and PassMark memory tests, while showing average results in multi-core processing and static web serving. Conversely, it exhibits weaker performance in CPU encryption benchmarks. This hardware profile is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, database operations, and memory-cached applications that do not demand local storage or heavy cryptographic processing.
